lesson.title: Four Score & Seven
lesson.subtitle: soixante-dix (60+10), quatre-vingts (4×20), and expressing age with avoir (j'ai trente ans).

hook.title: Counting by Twenties and Carrying Your Years
hook.content: Past sixty (soixante), French switches into its Celtic twenty-based gear: 70 is soixante-dix (60 + 10), 80 is quatre-vingts (4 × 20), 90 is quatre-vingt-dix (4 × 20 + 10), and 100 is cent! Combine these with J'ai… ans to state any age.

footnotes.title: Why quatre-vingts drops its -s when another number follows
footnotes.content: On 80 alone, quatre-vingts keeps the plural -s on vingts ('four twenties'). When another number follows (quatre-vingt-dix), vingt drops its -s!

pattern.content: Hear the arithmetic inside the number, and always pair ages with avoir + ans: Il a quatre-vingts ans ('He is eighty years old').
pattern.linguist_note: Vigesimal numeral composition (quatre-vingts) is an areal feature of Gallo-Romance.
pattern.trap_note: Never say *un cent for 'one hundred' — French says bare cent!

exercises.prompt: Match each higher French number with its arithmetic breakdown:
exercises.target_answer: thirty, sixty, seventy (70), eighty (80), one hundred (100)
exercises.meaning: trente (30), soixante (60), soixante-dix (60 + 10), quatre-vingts (4 × 20), cent (bare, no 'un'!)
exercises.explanation: 70 builds on 60; 80 and 90 build on four-twenties.

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word breakdown of 'quatre-vingts ans'?
How do you say 'one hundred euros' in French?
exercises.explanation: French never puts un before cent: bare cent euros!

exercises.idea: my father is sixty years old
cues: My father has sixty years → Mon père a soixante ans
exercises.meaning: My father is sixty years old

diagnosis.cue: Age always uses avoir: Mon père a soixante ans.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: C'est quatre-vingts euros, s'il vous plaît
exercises.target_answer: C'est quatre-vingts euros, s'il vous plaît
exercises.explanation: quatre-vingts keeps its -s when no smaller number follows.
exercises.affirmation: You spelled quatre-vingts with its hyphen and plural -s.

summary.outcome: Use trente, soixante, quatre-vingts, and cent in prices and ages with avoir.

use_example.english: My grandmother is eighty years old.

summary.takeaway: 70 is sixty-ten, 80 is four-twenties, and 100 is bare cent.

twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Mon père a soixante ans" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Four Score & Seven.

vingt.etymology_derivation: Latin vīgintī — English 'vigesimal' (counting by twenties) is the same root; French just kept counting that way: quatre-vingts.

quatre_vingts.etymology_derivation: Literally 'four-twenties', just like Abraham Lincoln's 'four score'. And 90 is quatre-vingt-dix ('four-twenty-ten')!

ans.context_translation: I'm thirty years old (I have thirty years).
ans.etymology_derivation: Latin annus — annual, anniversary. Age is something you have in French: j'ai X ans.

avoir.etymology_derivation: Latin habēre = have. The H dropped and stayed dropped — French never pronounces its Latin H.

jai.etymology_derivation: je + ai with the vowel sacrificed — elision again, the apostrophe marks the cut.
